title: C Introduction
summary: Write your first small C programs. Print a greeting, add two pencil counts and learn why a compiler is needed to run the code.
introduction: C is a language for giving steps to a computer. It is used in many tools and devices. You write a text file, then a compiler turns it into a program the computer can run. Start with a few short lines and check one change at a time.
learningObjectives: Print text and a whole number
Use an if statement to choose a step

rows: A tool that turns your C code into a program.
A named place for a value.
A named group of steps. main is where this program starts.

blocks.title: Where to run the examples
blocks.text: Read the [setup lesson](/tutorials/c/setup-compiler) to use C on your computer. These examples are shown here for reading; they do not run in this site playground.
stdio.h gives us printing tools. puts prints text and moves to a new line. The main function is where the program begins.
int stores a whole number. printf uses %d as a place for that number. The backslash-n makes a new line.

blocks.title: pencils.c

blocks.text: if runs its block only when the rule is true. Here 8 is at least 5, so the program prints the message.

blocks.title: score.c
Watch out
blocks.text: Most C statements end with a semicolon. Keep the quote marks around text. A missing symbol can stop the program from building.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: Change Asha to your name. Then change the pencil numbers and check the new total.
